intro: Hi! You already use the first conditional for real possibilities: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home. Today you imagine: dreams, wishes and situations that aren't real, like If I had more time, I would learn Japanese. You'll also give friendly advice with If I were you, and learn when to choose the first or the second conditional. Warm-up: how do you say 'seandainya saya punya lebih banyak waktu' in English?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: from b1-first-conditional the learner knows if + present simple, will + base verb for real possibilities (If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home), no will after if, and unless / as soon as / in case; from a2-past-simple-irregular the past forms (had, knew, won, lost). They also know would from the phrase I'd like / Would you like ...? (a1-like-would-like). New: second conditional = if + past simple, would / 'd + base verb, for situations that are imagined, unlikely or impossible now or in the future: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese (= I don't have more time). Negative wouldn't; question What would you do if ...?; the if-part can come first (comma) or second (no comma).

Always say why the past form doesn't mean past time, so it never looks like a broken rule: here the past form shows distance from reality (jauh dari kenyataan, tidak nyata), not yesterday. If I had a car = I don't have a car now. Indonesian marks this with a word (seandainya, andaikan, kalau saja) and keeps the verb; English marks it by moving the verb to the past and using would in the result. Indonesian 'akan' covers both will and would, so learners write will in the result.

Common errors and why: *'If I would have more money, I would buy a car' -> 'If I had more money, I would buy a car' (no would in the if-part, just as there's no will after if in the first conditional). *'If I have a lot of money, I would travel the world' -> 'If I had a lot of money, ...' (don't mix: present + will for real, past + would for imagined). *'If I were you, I will talk to her' -> 'If I were you, I would / I'd talk to her'. Also *'would bought' / *'would to buy' (would + base verb, no to).

If I were you, I'd ... = advice, like You should ... but more personal (Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan ...). Negative advice: If I were you, I wouldn't .... were is the standard form for every person after if (If I were you, If she were here, If it were cheaper). 'If I was you / If she was here' is common in casual speech: mention it only as a note, don't treat it as a serious error in speaking, but teach and test were.

First vs second: first = a real possibility or plan (If it rains tomorrow, ...; If I get the job, ...) -> kalau. Second = imagined, unlikely or impossible now (If I won the lottery, ...; If I were taller, ...; If I lived by the sea, ... when you don't) -> seandainya. Everyday Indonesian kalau can be used for both, so the learner should ask 'real or imagined?', not translate the word. Only test cases where the context decides clearly (the person doesn't have it or can't change it vs. a real plan or a forecast). Some sentences can take both forms with a different feeling (If I win / If I won the competition): don't test those, but explain the feeling if a learner asks.

Limits: no third conditional (If I had known, I would have ...), no would have, no wish / if only, no mixed conditionals, no past perfect. could / might in the result (If I had a car, I could drive you) are fine if the learner uses them, but aren't taught here. If a learner asks, say these come in later lessons. B1 contexts: office, KRL, ojek online, Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, rupiah, job offers, salaries, kos.

keyPoints.title: Imagine: if + past simple, would + base verb
keyPoints.explanation: For situations that aren't real now, or are very unlikely in the future: if + past simple, would ('d) + base verb. The past form doesn't mean yesterday here: it shows the situation is not real (jauh dari kenyataan). If I had more time = I don't have more time. No would in the if-part ('If I would have' is wrong), and be becomes were: If I were rich.

examples.en: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
examples.id: Seandainya saya punya lebih banyak waktu, saya akan belajar bahasa Jepang.

examples.en: If Rina lived in Bandung, she'd visit her parents every weekend.
examples.id: Seandainya Rina tinggal di Bandung, dia akan mengunjungi orang tuanya setiap akhir pekan.

examples.en: What would you do if you lost your phone?
examples.id: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan seandainya HP-mu hilang?

id.title: Berandai-andai: if + past simple, would + kata kerja dasar
id.explanation: Untuk situasi yang tidak nyata sekarang, atau sangat kecil kemungkinannya di masa depan: if + past simple, would ('d) + kata kerja dasar. Bentuk past di sini bukan berarti kemarin: bentuk ini menunjukkan situasinya tidak nyata (jauh dari kenyataan). If I had more time = saya tidak punya lebih banyak waktu. Tidak ada would di bagian if ('If I would have' salah), dan be berubah jadi were: If I were rich.

keyPoints.title: Advice: If I were you, I'd ...
keyPoints.explanation: To give advice, imagine you are the other person: If I were you, I would / I'd + base verb (= Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan ...). It means the same as You should ..., but sounds more personal. Negative: If I were you, I wouldn't .... The result needs would, not will. You also hear 'If I was you' in casual speech, but were is the standard form.

examples.en: If I were you, I'd talk to your manager.
examples.id: Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan bicara dengan manajermu.

examples.en: If I were you, I wouldn't lend him money again.
examples.id: Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya tidak akan meminjamkan uang lagi kepadanya.

examples.en: I'd take the KRL if I were you. The traffic is terrible today.
examples.id: Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan naik KRL. Hari ini macetnya parah.

id.title: Saran: If I were you, I'd ...
id.explanation: Untuk memberi saran, bayangkan kamu menjadi orang itu: If I were you, I would / I'd + kata kerja dasar (= Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan ...). Artinya sama dengan You should ..., tapi terdengar lebih akrab. Negatif: If I were you, I wouldn't .... Bagian hasilnya perlu would, bukan will. Saat bicara santai kamu juga akan dengar 'If I was you', tapi were adalah bentuk bakunya.

keyPoints.title: Real or imagined? First vs second conditional
keyPoints.explanation: First conditional (if + present, will) = a real possibility or plan: it can really happen (kalau). Second conditional (if + past, would) = imagined: a dream, very unlikely, or impossible now (seandainya). Ask yourself: is it real, or am I imagining?

examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home.
examples.id: Kalau besok hujan, kita di rumah saja. (bisa terjadi)

examples.en: If I won the lottery, I'd buy my parents a house.
examples.id: Seandainya saya menang lotre, saya akan membelikan orang tua saya rumah. (mimpi)

examples.en: If I get the job in Surabaya, I'll move there in May.
examples.id: Kalau saya dapat pekerjaan di Surabaya, saya akan pindah ke sana bulan Mei. (rencana nyata)

id.title: Nyata atau khayalan? First vs second conditional
id.explanation: First conditional (if + present, will) = kemungkinan nyata atau rencana: bisa benar-benar terjadi (kalau). Second conditional (if + past, would) = khayalan: mimpi, sangat kecil kemungkinannya, atau tidak mungkin sekarang (seandainya). Tanyakan pada dirimu: ini nyata, atau saya sedang berandai-andai?

assessment.prompt: Dimas doesn't have a car, so he takes the KRL to work every day. Complete with the verb in brackets: If he ___ (have) a car, he would drive to work.
acceptableAnswers: had
if he had a car he would drive to work
if he had a car he'd drive to work
assessment.rubric: Correct: had (he doesn't have a car, so the if-part is imagined: past simple). 'has' = 0 (that's for a real possibility with will, and it doesn't match would). 'would have' = 0 (no would in the if-part).

assessment.prompt: Sari doesn't speak Japanese, but her company has a job for her in Tokyo. Complete with would and the verb in brackets: If she spoke Japanese, she ___ (apply) for the job.
acceptableAnswers: would apply
'd apply
if she spoke japanese she would apply for the job
if she spoke japanese she'd apply for the job
assessment.rubric: Correct: would apply / 'd apply. 'would applied' or 'would to apply' = 50 (would + base verb). 'will apply' = 30 (the if-part is imagined, so the result needs would). 'applied' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: If I would know her address, I would send her a wedding present.

i'd send her a wedding present if i knew her address

assessment.prompt: Your friend Sari goes to bed at 2 a.m. every night and she's always tired at work. Give her advice. Start with If I were you and use: go to bed earlier.

i would go to bed earlier if i were you
i'd go to bed earlier if i were you
assessment.rubric: Correct: If I were you, I'd / I would go to bed earlier. 'If I was you, I'd go to bed earlier' = 80 (common in casual speech, but were is the standard form). 'If I were you, I will go ...' = 40 (the result needs would). 'If I were you, I go ...' = 40. 'You should go to bed earlier' = 50 (good advice, but the item asks for If I were you).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: If I were you, I will take the job in Surabaya.

if i were you i'd take the job in surabaya
i would take the job in surabaya if i were you
i'd take the job in surabaya if i were you

assessment.prompt:

b if i lived in bali i'd go swimming every morning
if i lived in bali i'd go swimming every morning
if i lived in bali i would go swimming every morning
assessment.rubric: Correct: B (living in Bali is impossible for him now: imagined, so if + past, would). A = 0 (the first conditional is for real possibilities).

assessment.prompt: The sky is very dark and the weather app says heavy rain this afternoon. Complete with the verbs in brackets: If it ___ (rain), we ___ (cancel) the futsal match.

'rained ... would cancel' = 30 (correct form, but this situation is real, not imagined). 'will rain ... will cancel' = 40 (no will after if). 'rains ... would cancel' = 20 (mixes the two conditionals).

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** the first conditional is for **real** possibilities: *If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* (if + present, will)

Now something new: situations that are **not real**: a dream, a wish, something impossible now or very unlikely. For these, English uses the **second conditional**:
- **if + past simple** (*had, lived, knew, won*)
- **would + base verb** (*kata kerja dasar*, the verb without -s, -ed or to)

*If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.*

**would** isn't new: you know it from *I'd like* and *Would you like …?*. Here it means *akan* in an imagined world. Short form: **'d** (*I'd, you'd, she'd, we'd, they'd*). Negative: **wouldn't** (= would not). Question: **What would you do if …?**

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** first conditional dipakai untuk kemungkinan yang **nyata**: *If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* (if + present, will)

Sekarang hal baru: situasi yang **tidak nyata**: mimpi, keinginan, sesuatu yang tidak mungkin sekarang atau sangat kecil kemungkinannya. Untuk ini, bahasa Inggris memakai **second conditional**:
- **if + past simple** (*had, lived, knew, won*)
- **would + kata kerja dasar** (kata kerja tanpa -s, -ed atau to)

*If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.*

**would** bukan hal baru: kamu sudah kenal dari *I'd like* dan *Would you like …?*. Di sini artinya *akan* di dunia khayalan. Bentuk pendek: **'d** (*I'd, you'd, she'd, we'd, they'd*). Negatif: **wouldn't** (= would not). Pertanyaan: **What would you do if …?**

blocks.text:
**Why the past? It's not about yesterday.** *If I had more time* is about **now**. The past form shows the situation is **not real**, far from reality (*jauh dari kenyataan*): I **don't** have more time. Think of the verb taking one step back from reality.
Indonesian shows this with a word (*seandainya, andaikan, kalau saja*) and the verb doesn't change. English shows it with the **verb**: it moves to the past, and the result uses **would**.

id.text:
**Kenapa pakai past? Ini bukan soal kemarin.** *If I had more time* itu tentang **sekarang**. Bentuk past menunjukkan situasinya **tidak nyata**, *jauh dari kenyataan*: saya **tidak** punya lebih banyak waktu. Bayangkan kata kerjanya mundur satu langkah dari kenyataan.
Bahasa Indonesia menunjukkannya dengan kata (*seandainya, andaikan, kalau saja*) dan kata kerjanya tidak berubah. Bahasa Inggris menunjukkannya lewat **kata kerja**: pindah ke bentuk past, dan bagian hasilnya memakai **would**.

rows.en: If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
rows.id: Seandainya saya punya lebih banyak waktu, saya akan belajar bahasa Jepang.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan says: 'If I had a bigger house, my parents would live with us.' Does Pak Hasan have a bigger house?
options: Yes, he had one in the past.
No, he doesn't have one now.
blocks.explain: *If I had* is about now, and the past form shows it's **not real**: he doesn't have a bigger house. It isn't about the past.

id.prompt: Pak Hasan berkata: 'If I had a bigger house, my parents would live with us.' Apakah Pak Hasan punya rumah yang lebih besar?
id.explain: *If I had* itu tentang sekarang, dan bentuk past menunjukkan bahwa itu **tidak nyata**: dia tidak punya rumah yang lebih besar. Ini bukan tentang masa lalu.

blocks.text:
**Trap 1: no would in the if-part.** *would* goes only in the result part, just like *will* in the first conditional (*If it rains*, not 'If it will rain').
- 'If I would have more money, I would buy a car.' is wrong → **If I had more money, I would buy a car.**

**Trap 2: don't mix the two conditionals.** Keep the pairs together: **if + present → will** (real), **if + past → would** (imagined).
- 'If I have a lot of money, I would travel the world.' is wrong → **If I had a lot of money, I would travel the world.**

Why do Indonesian speakers make these mistakes? *akan* means both **will** and **would**, and *seandainya saya punya* has no past. So check the if-part: past → **would** in the result.

id.text:
**Jebakan 1: tidak ada would di bagian if.** *would* hanya ada di bagian hasil, sama seperti *will* di first conditional (*If it rains*, bukan 'If it will rain').
- 'If I would have more money, I would buy a car.' salah → **If I had more money, I would buy a car.**

**Jebakan 2: jangan campur dua conditional.** Pasangannya tetap: **if + present → will** (nyata), **if + past → would** (khayalan).
- 'If I have a lot of money, I would travel the world.' salah → **If I had a lot of money, I would travel the world.**

Kenapa orang Indonesia sering salah di sini? *akan* berarti **will** sekaligus **would**, dan *seandainya saya punya* tidak punya bentuk past. Jadi cek bagian if: past → **would** di bagian hasil.

blocks.text:
**be → were for everyone.** After *if* in an imagined situation, use **were** for every person: *If I were rich …, If she were here …, If it were cheaper …*. It looks strange because you learnt *I was*, but it's a special form for imagined situations.
In casual speech many people (British and American) say *If I was / If she was*. In writing, at work and in tests, use **were**.

id.text:
**be → were untuk semua subjek.** Sesudah *if* dalam situasi khayalan, pakai **were** untuk semua subjek: *If I were rich …, If she were here …, If it were cheaper …*. Kelihatannya aneh karena kamu belajar *I was*, tapi ini bentuk khusus untuk situasi khayalan.
Saat bicara santai, banyak orang (British dan American) bilang *If I was / If she was*. Dalam tulisan, di kantor dan dalam tes, pakai **were**.

blocks.prompt: If my company ___ me a day off, I would go to my cousin's wedding.
blocks.explain: The result has **would**, so the if-part is imagined: **past simple (gave)**. *would* never goes in the if-part, and *gives* goes with *will*, not would.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: If my company ___ me a day off, I would go to my cousin's wedding.
id.explain: Bagian hasil memakai **would**, jadi bagian if adalah khayalan: **past simple (gave)**. *would* tidak pernah ada di bagian if, dan *gives* berpasangan dengan *will*, bukan would.

material.title: Advice: If I were you, I'd …

blocks.text:
To give advice, imagine you **are** the other person: **If I were you, I'd (I would) + base verb** = *Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan …*. I'm not you, so it's imagined: a second conditional. It means the same as **You should …**, but sounds friendlier and more personal.
- Negative advice: **If I were you, I wouldn't …**
- It can also go at the end: **I'd … if I were you.** (no comma)

id.text:
Untuk memberi saran, bayangkan kamu **menjadi** orang itu: **If I were you, I'd (I would) + kata kerja dasar** = *Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan …*. Saya bukan kamu, jadi ini khayalan: second conditional. Artinya sama dengan **You should …**, tapi terdengar lebih ramah dan akrab.
- Saran negatif: **If I were you, I wouldn't …**
- Bisa juga di akhir kalimat: **I'd … if I were you.** (tanpa koma)

rows.en: If I were you, I'd talk to your manager.
rows.id: Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan bicara dengan manajermu.

rows.en: If I were you, I wouldn't lend him money again.
rows.id: Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya tidak akan meminjamkan uang lagi kepadanya.

rows.en: I'd take the KRL if I were you. The traffic is terrible today.
rows.id: Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan naik KRL. Hari ini macetnya parah.
rows.note: if-part at the end: no comma

id.note: bagian if di akhir: tanpa koma

rows.en: If I were you, I'd ask for a higher salary.
rows.id: Kalau saya jadi kamu, saya akan minta gaji yang lebih tinggi.

blocks.text:
**Trap:** 'If I were you, I will talk to her.' is wrong → **If I were you, I'd talk to her.** The if-part is imagined, so the result needs **would**, not will.
**were or was?** *If I was you* is common in casual speech, but **If I were you** is the standard form: use it in writing, at work and in tests.

id.text:
**Jebakan:** 'If I were you, I will talk to her.' salah → **If I were you, I'd talk to her.** Bagian if-nya khayalan, jadi bagian hasil perlu **would**, bukan will.
**were atau was?** *If I was you* sering terdengar saat bicara santai, tapi **If I were you** adalah bentuk bakunya: pakai dalam tulisan, di kantor dan dalam tes.

blocks.prompt: Your friend Budi wants to buy an expensive phone with his credit card, but he already has a lot of debt. Which advice is correct?
options: If I were you, I wouldn't buy it.
If I were you, I won't buy it.
If I would be you, I wouldn't buy it.
blocks.explain: **If I were you** + **wouldn't** + base verb. *won't* (will not) doesn't match an imagined if-part, and *would* never goes after *if*.

id.prompt: Temanmu Budi mau membeli HP mahal dengan kartu kreditnya, padahal utangnya sudah banyak. Saran mana yang benar?
id.explain: **If I were you** + **wouldn't** + kata kerja dasar. *won't* (will not) tidak cocok dengan bagian if yang khayalan, dan *would* tidak pernah ada sesudah *if*.

id.title: Saran: If I were you, I'd …

material.title: Real or imagined? First vs second

blocks.text:
Both conditionals talk about the present or the future. The difference is **how real** the situation is:
- **First conditional** (if + present, will) = a **real possibility**: it can really happen. Indonesian: *kalau / jika*.
- **Second conditional** (if + past, would) = **imagined**: a dream, very unlikely, or impossible now. Indonesian: *seandainya / andaikan*.

**Quick test:** do you know it's **not true** now (I'm not rich, I don't live there, I can't be taller)? Use the second. Is it a real plan, or something that may really happen (a forecast, an interview tomorrow)? Use the first.

id.text:
Kedua conditional membicarakan sekarang atau masa depan. Bedanya adalah **seberapa nyata** situasinya:
- **First conditional** (if + present, will) = **kemungkinan nyata**: bisa benar-benar terjadi. Bahasa Indonesia: *kalau / jika*.
- **Second conditional** (if + past, would) = **khayalan**: mimpi, sangat kecil kemungkinannya, atau tidak mungkin sekarang. Bahasa Indonesia: *seandainya / andaikan*.

**Tes cepat:** kamu tahu itu **tidak benar** sekarang (saya tidak kaya, saya tidak tinggal di sana, saya tidak bisa jadi lebih tinggi)? Pakai second. Itu rencana nyata, atau sesuatu yang memang bisa terjadi (prakiraan cuaca, wawancara besok)? Pakai first.

rows.en: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home.
rows.id: Kalau besok hujan, kita di rumah saja.

rows.en: If I get the job in Surabaya, I'll move there in May.

rows.en: If I won the lottery, I'd buy my parents a house.

rows.id: Seandainya kantor saya di Bandung, saya akan naik gunung setiap akhir pekan.

blocks.text:
**Careful with kalau.** In everyday Indonesian, *kalau* is used for both (*Kalau saya kaya, …*). So don't translate the word: ask **real or imagined?**
**Same idea, different feeling:** *If I win the competition, I'll …* (I think I have a real chance) and *If I won the competition, I'd …* (just dreaming) are both correct. The speaker shows how real it feels.

id.text:
**Hati-hati dengan kalau.** Dalam bahasa sehari-hari, *kalau* dipakai untuk keduanya (*Kalau saya kaya, …*). Jadi jangan terjemahkan katanya: tanyakan **nyata atau khayalan?**
**Ide sama, rasa berbeda:** *If I win the competition, I'll …* (saya merasa punya peluang nyata) dan *If I won the competition, I'd …* (cuma berkhayal) sama-sama benar. Pembicara menunjukkan seberapa nyata rasanya.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is about something imagined, not a real plan?
options: If I get a bonus this month, I'll take my family to the beach.
If I were a millionaire, I'd never work again.
If it's sunny on Sunday, I'll go to the beach.
blocks.explain: *If I were a millionaire* = I'm not one: **imagined**, so if + past, would. The other two can really happen (a bonus, sunny weather): if + present, will.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang tentang khayalan, bukan rencana nyata?
id.explain: *If I were a millionaire* = saya bukan jutawan: **khayalan**, jadi if + past, would. Dua kalimat lainnya bisa benar-benar terjadi (bonus, cuaca cerah): if + present, will.

id.intro: Hai! Kamu sudah memakai first conditional untuk kemungkinan nyata: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home. Hari ini kamu berandai-andai: mimpi, keinginan dan situasi yang tidak nyata, seperti If I had more time, I would learn Japanese. Kamu juga akan memberi saran dengan If I were you, dan belajar kapan memilih first atau second conditional. Pemanasan: apa bahasa Inggrisnya 'seandainya saya punya lebih banyak waktu'?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa kita pakai bentuk past (had, lived) padahal membicarakan sekarang?
Bolehkah saya bilang 'If I was you', bukan 'If I were you'?
Apa bedanya 'If I win' dan 'If I won'?
Apakah 'If I were you, I'd …' sama dengan 'You should …'?

assessment.sec-1: Dimas tidak punya mobil, jadi dia naik KRL ke kantor setiap hari. Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: If he ___ (have) a car, he would drive to work.
assessment.sec-2: Sari tidak bisa bahasa Jepang, tapi kantornya punya lowongan untuknya di Tokyo. Lengkapi dengan would dan kata kerja dalam kurung: If she spoke Japanese, she ___ (apply) for the job.
assessment.sec-3: Perbaiki kesalahannya: If I would know her address, I would send her a wedding present.
assessment.sec-4: Temanmu Sari tidur jam 2 pagi setiap malam dan dia selalu capek di kantor. Beri dia saran dalam bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan If I were you dan pakai: go to bed earlier.
assessment.sec-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: If I were you, I will take the job in Surabaya.
assessment.sec-6:
Pak Hasan tinggal dan bekerja di Jakarta. Dia suka laut, tapi pindah ke Bali tidak mungkin baginya sekarang. Kalimat mana yang cocok? Jawab A atau B.
A: If I live in Bali, I'll go swimming every morning.
B: If I lived in Bali, I'd go swimming every morning.
assessment.sec-7: Langit sangat gelap dan aplikasi cuaca bilang sore ini akan hujan deras. Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: If it ___ (rain), we ___ (cancel) the futsal match.
